recipes.name: Spicy Red Bell Pepper Soup
ingredients_raw: 6 red bell peppers, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Stir in bell peppers, onions, carrots, celery, and garlic; cook and stir until vegetables soft, about 10 minutes. Stir in chicken broth, rice, thyme, salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper, and red pepper flakes; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until rice and vegetables tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from heat; cool 30 minutes.
Purée cooled soup with an immersion blender until smooth. Or use a blender and purée, in batches, until smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Red Bell Pepper Soup
raw_recipe.description: Fresh red bell peppers blended with celery, carrots, onion, thyme, and rice take on a little heat from cayenne and red pepper flakes in this colorful, chicken-stock based soup.

review.reviewBody: This was GREAT! I doubled the spices, since we like things hot, and used brown rice. Served with some toasted rye croutons and a tiny wedge of chili-lime gouda for garnish. Raves from my guests!

Very good! I was a little skeptical about using rice as a thickener, but it worked beautifully. This is also a great recipe for using up any extra veggies that are hanging around the fridge. I garnished this with shrimp and peppers, very pretty. Thanks!

The base recipe is great for sure! We like more spice in my household so amped it up that way. Also added shrimp that I sautéed in some Cajun seasoning. Definitely a go to recipe. So easy amd fun to make. Thank you

I followed this recipe because I had 2 pounds of small red and yellow peppers that I needed to use. This recipe came out great. I also used 4 carrots and skipped the celery. I also added about 12 ounces of mushrooms. I did not puree the soup. This was an excellent soup to serve on a hot summer afternoon.

Hi

I first roasted my peppers, it gives awesome flavor, and the the rice did not do it for me, so I used red lentils.

I have made this several times now. Full disclosure: I have altered the recipe based on a review that felt it lacked something; it was good, but flat. Looking at the ingredients, I felt it probably needed a little sour/acid what with all the sweet going on, so I added a lemon slice with the broth (removing it prior to blending!) and reasoned that if the peppers were fresh, why not add a fresh hot pepper, serrano, instead of the cayenne and red pepper flakes. Additionally, because I didn't have any fresh or dried thyme, I added some mint. I am really liking this soup, you should try it!

This soup is called "spicy" in the title, and several reviewers complained that it was too spicy. I made this recipe per the instructions...and was underwhelmed. There was no heat, to my taste buds, which meant that to my husband's taste buds, it was going to taste like I was serving him a big bowl of "Bland Stuff I Hate Soup". So I added pre-cooked plain chicken, shredded (because I had planned to anyway), and many generous spoonfuls of Sriracha (Asian-style hot sauce). It was still missing something, so I added lemon juice until it seemed...bright. (No, I can't really explain "bright taste" any better.) I pureed this soup with my immersion blender, because my husband-who-loves-things-spicy is also a guy-who-hates-cooked-vegetable-textures. Overall, we ate it, and will finish the pot over the next day or so, but I probably wouldn't make this again unless I had a lot of bell peppers to use up! Thanks for the recipe though, I really enjoyed making this one :) (P.S. If you want to use brown rice, just bring the soup to a boil after you add it, then turn it down to low and cook for the amount of time specified on your brand of rice's package--or about 15 minutes less if you're going to puree the soup.)

I used this recipe as a base idea for spiced soup as part of our fast 800 diet , my wife has bee a bit ill with flu and a nasty cough I used two small red bell peppers and 1 carrot celery sta instead of chilli flakes ,I grated a little frozen scotch bonnet , basically I followed the recipe ...it was delicious and fiery hot. My wife reckons it hs burned out her sore throat and reduced the coughing I will make this again definitely ,maybe a little less scotch bonnet next time

I added lime juice, a pinch of cumin and sugar and since I had some marina sauce (instead of fresh tomatoes), it turned out great. However, I did not use any celery. I am having guests and will serve some sour cream if they want to top it off with. I also made some homemade bread to serve with it. I will make this again.

I really enjoyed this recipe! I gave it four stars, because , like many of the others that have reviewed this soup, I had to slightly tweek it. I substituted quinoa for the white rice. After simmering for the directed 25 minutes, I added a dash of cumin and chili powder based on how it smelled. Before blending, I also added a few teaspoons on lemon juice as recommended by several other reviews. I do not like celery, so that was cut. Overall, the spice was perfect and the consistency was surprisingly creamy (given there is no dairy). I think this would actually be great with a grilled cheese instead of tomato soup.

I make this all the time. It's so delicious I forgo dessert and eat another bowl of it. I add more garlic than the recipe calls for. I use hot paprika instead of Cayenne and I often forget the red pepper flakes! The soup tastes sweet and spicy, a perfect blend. Speaking of blending, sometimes I don't. I eat the soup with the diced pieces. A different mouth feel but just as delicious.
Great recipe, changed the rice to red lentils
Spicy but delicious! Didn’t have any celery but still turned out yummy!

My family loves this soup! We like to shop at Aldi and they have those 3 packs of red, yellow, and orange peppers, so we decided to try the recipe with 6 assorted peppers instead of 6 red peppers. It turned out just as good :)

I haven't blended it yet but I just finished cooking. I sauteed the peppers and vegetables a LOT longer than the recipe called for, basically until they were caramelized. I wasn't paying attention but it was probably an hour. Then the broth went in and it cooked for another 35 minutes. I guess the secret is lots of free time and patience. It came out so good! 10/10 I will make again if I have a good bit of time to kill :)

I skipped the celery although I know it’s traditional to have the full mire poix… it was so good that we had no leftovers! I made a half a recipe hoping to pack for lunch the next day and my boyfriend went back for the last in the stockpot! Next time I will put the extra in freezer containers as soon as I serve everyone LOL! Fresh flavor and quick to prepare. Garnished with a little shredded cheese.
This reciipe is so easy to make! I added a bit more rice, 1/4 cup extra, and I added no salt as the broth was salty enough. I will definitely be making this again!

I had leftover red pepper chili. Not enough to make a jar so I threw the peppers that I had left and because it was already spiced. Now my soup is a little over spiced so I cut it with milk. It is so good. Still spicy
Good, favorable soup. For those complaining the soup is too bland, perhaps try a different chicken stock?

I was trying to use up some green bell peppers from the garden, and a couple yellow/orange ones in the fridge that were on the way out. This recipe called for a lot of peppers—so, YAY! I did cut the recipe in half, though, because it was the first time, and if we didn’t like it, I didn’t want a ton. But it was fan-tas-tic!!! I will be making it again—and in the full quantity! I love how the rice is the thickener.
